slides.0.title: Old vines, single vineyards and special schemes
slides.0.subtitle: The Old Vine Project and labelling
slides.1.title: The Old Vine Project
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Origins
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Driven by vineyard manager Rosa Kruger from 2002 and formalised in 2016 with seed funding from the Rupert Foundation
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The 35-year threshold
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Vineyards must be 35 years or older, with the planting date given at application; SAWIS records planting dates back to 1900
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Certified Heritage Vineyards seal
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The seal assures consumers the wine is authentic and made to OVP viticultural and winemaking guidelines; the densest concentration of certified parcels is in the Swartland
slides.1.content: The OVP protects old vines and makes them visible to consumers; it is not a new WO tier.
slides.2.title: Seals and traceability
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The combined WO and IPW seal
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A combined WO and IPW seal has been available since the 2010 harvest; in 2024, 88% of certified wines carried it
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Checkable
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Buyers can verify origin, variety, vintage, producer and bottling data at sawis.co.za using the seal number
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Unregulated terms
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Reserve, Grand Reserve and Limited Edition have no legal quality meaning; whether a term like "old vines" is backed depends on OVP certification
slides.2.content: When reading a South African label, check the seal, WO tier, variety and vintage percentages first, then weigh voluntary terms.
What minimum vine age does the Old Vine Project require?
In which year was the OVP formalised with Rupert Foundation seed funding?
2016; 2002 is when Rosa Kruger began the work.
What legal meaning does "Reserve" have on a South African label?
A. At least two years' ageing
